title: A new protocol for live imaging of mammalian retina _ex vivo_ by confocal laser scanning microscopy
protocol: Obtain freshly enucleated bovine eyes from a local slaughterhouse within 1.5 hours of animal death.
Cut eyes in half and divide the eyeballs into two eyecups.
Carefully remove the cornea, lens, and vitreous and discard them.
Fill the semi-cup containing choroid and retina still attached to the RPE with 6-9 ml of MR solution containing 2 mM glucose, protease inhibitor cocktail, and Ampicillin (100 μg/ml).
Incubate for 5-10 minutes.
If necessary, add appropriate inhibitors to test dye specificity.
Conduct all steps in dim red light.
Add mitochondrial vital dyes from a stock solution to the eye semicup solution.
Incubate in the dark for 10-15 minutes without washing the eye semicups.
Mount the sample for imaging using option A or B based on preference.
For option A, after 20 minutes of incubation, shake the eye semicup gently to detach retinas from pigmented epithelium.
Remove retinas by turning the eye semi-cup inside out and cutting the retina free from the optic nerve.
Mount detached retinas onto a coverslip for CLSM without washing or fixing them.
For option B, set overall incubation time to no more than 10 minutes if rods must remain embedded in RPE.
Cut at the rim all around the posterior eye semi-cup.
Mount the posterior eye semi-cup on a coverslip chamber with the retina facing downwards.
Alternatively, immerse the whole semi-cup in a small pool arranged over the immersion objective of the microscope.
Wrap the immersion objective carefully in a plastic glove and allow its tip to emerge through a small hole.
Hold the eye-semicup while the objective moves up and down to reach proper focal planes.
Image the labelled retinas using CLSM at 23°C.
Acquire measurements with a Leica TCS SP5-AOBS inverted confocal laser scanning microscope equipped with 457-476-488-514-543-633 nm laser lines.
Examine specimens using an HCX APO L U-V-I 63x/0.9NA water immersion objective.
Cut the whole semicup at the rim and mount onto the coverslip chamber if retinas are left in the eye-semicup.
Immerse the whole semicup in a small pool arranged around the objective if the retina is detached from the choroid.
Hold the eye-semicup while moving the objective up and down to reach proper focal planes.
Excite retinas stained with MitoTracker Deep Red 633 at 633 nm.
Collect emission in the spectral range from 650 to 700nm.
Keep laser power and detection settings equal across all experiments.
Acquire, store, and visualize resulting images with Leica Confocal Software.
Carry out image elaboration, analysis, and three-dimensional rendering by ImageJ software.
